thread:
jen: Hey team, escalated ticket #INC-8423 from AcmeGames — users can't finish OAuth with Google. They see a 400 on the callback with `invalid_request` and `state` mismatch. Repro steps in ticket.

olivia: pinging from CS — customer started seeing this after we rolled the new CDN in front of their app yesterday. GitHub logins mostly work; Google fails ~95% of the time.

jen: TL;DR from support: redirect URI is correct in console, PKCE flow used, state param arrives shorter at our callback endpoint than the one we sent to Google. Looks like chars trimmed. Suspect encoding/proxy trimming.

kai: Can we get the exact redirect URL they send to Google? any non-ascii chars in state? emoji maybe? I've seen cookie/proxy rules choke on certain percent-encoded sequences.

olivia: Customer pasted the initial auth URL in the ticket: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Facme.example.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=openid%20email&state=%F0%9F%98%8A-7f3a2b&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256

jen: That state contains a smiley emoji (U+1F60A) -> percent-encoded as %F0%9F%98%8A. If something in the chain treats the percent sign specially or truncates after %F0, mismatch can happen.

rahul: On our callback logs I see incoming queries where state is "-7f3a2b" (emoji bytes dropped). Example from ingress logs:
```
GET /oauth/callback?code=4/AA...&state=-7f3a2b
Host: acme.example.com
User-Agent: Google
```
So the prefix percent-encoded bytes are gone.

kai: That matches garbage-in from an intermediate proxy. Any WAF or Cloudflare worker that decodes + re-encodes URL parts? Some proxies have max header/query length or strip percent sequences.

jen: Customer says they put a Cloudflare Worker (edge) with a snippet to normalize paths. They also said they replaced `encodeURIComponent` with a custom routine for legacy browsers.

olivia: Customer repro steps they sent:
1) Click "Sign in with Google" on mobile web (iOS 16 Safari)
2) Popup -> Google auth -> redirects back to acme.example.com/oauth/callback
3) Immediately see 400 with "state did not match"

jen: Logged the customer's user-agent: `Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_4 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/16.4 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1`

kai: Two action items for us:
- (A) add defensive handling: if incoming state is a suffix of any pending state in the session store, accept and log as tolerant fallback for 48h. Help customers while they fix edge.
- (B) find where truncation happens — ask Acme to bypass Cloudflare worker or show worker code.

rahul: I can add (A) quickly: lookup by suffix match and attach telemetry label `oauth_state_suffix_accepted` when matched. Will need product signoff for security tradeoff though (short window + logs). I'll draft a PR.

jen: Meanwhile ask customer for worker code and example of full outgoing URL + captured callback URL (they already provided both, but we need the worker snippet). Olivia, can you get the worker code and whether they use `decodeURIComponent` anywhere?

olivia: Yep; they just posted the worker handler:
```
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  event.respondWith(handle(event.request))
})

async function handle(req) {
  let url = new URL(req.url)
  // normalize to remove trailing slash
  url.pathname = url.pathname.replace(/\\/+$/, '')
  return fetch(url.toString(), req)
}
```
They strip trailing slashes via regex, but note the `fetch(url.toString(), req)` passes the original `Request` object — might cause double-encoding/decoding differences.

kai: I suspect `url.toString()` will produce decoded components for some sequences depending on host runtime. Worker might normalize percent-encoded sequences which drops non-UTF-8-preserving bytes. Also the regex `\/+ $` seems fine, but they aren't preserving original query encoding carefully.

jen: Also customer confirmed they do `state = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({u:uid,nonce:random(),emoji: '😊'}))` on client. So emoji definitely enters state.

rahul: For quick mitigation I can implement suffix-accept with strict constraints: only allow if suffix length >= 8 hex chars and session has recent pending state. Log full original header raw query into a safe store for debugging (masked). I'll raise PR with tests.

kai: Long term fix: update best-practice docs to recommend base64url encoding of PKCE/state payloads (no percent-encoded emoji). Add a lint rule in our quickstart that warns on raw encodeURIComponent usage for state when non-ascii content present.

jen: Customer-side fix: remove emoji from state or use base64url. Ask them to test bypassing Cloudflare worker by pointing subdomain at the origin for a test path.

olivia: I asked them to try a bypass and they said "bypass works: state intact when worker disabled". So confirmed worker is culprit.

kai: Good. For our side: (1) rahul implements tolerant suffix lookup and telemetry, (2) I will add a warning in the next SDK release to recommend base64url encoding for state PKCE, (3) ops team to update docs.

rahul: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/941 — implements suffix acceptance behind feature flag `feature.oauth_state_tolerant_accept`. Tests included. Will request review from kai.

jen: Customer update sent: "thanks — we disabled worker and users can log in again. We'll push a worker fix next week." They asked for rollout ETA on our change to accept suffixes.

kai: If PR approved today, we can ship to staging tomorrow, behind flag, enable for 10% traffic after smoke tests. ETA to prod ~72h if no issues.

olivia: Customer asked about security implications: any risk of accepting partial state? They want to know we won't open replay vectors.

rahul: Mitigation: only accept suffix when there's an exact match on user session pending state (not any recent). We check PKCE code_verifier pairing and nonce in state. Only accept if code maps to same session id and lifetime < 2 minutes. Documented in PR.

jen: Nice. I'll keep ticket INC-8423 updated and mark as "in progress". Thanks all.

auth-bot: Incident note created INC-8423: oauth-state-truncation — assigned to jen, rahul, kai.

jen: Closing loop: once feature goes live we'll notify Acme and offer to re-enable worker and test together. :thumbsup:
